exposure_policy.formula: EV100 = log2(f_number**2 * shutter_speed) at ISO 100; shutter_for_ev(ev) = 2**(ev - log2(f_number**2))
exposure_policy.iso_note: READ BACK LIVE as 100.0. The parameter key is :ISO, not :iso - pass 1 read nil from :iso and had to assume ISO 100, so its EV numbers were derived. They are now measured.

render_quality_settings.cost: render 01 362.1 s and render 02 361.4 s at 1200x900, against pass 1's single 148.6 s render at 1200x900 on stock settings with no denoiser - about 2.4x. Image rows are unchanged at well under a second each.
render_quality_settings.honest_caveat: BOTH renders ran out the 6-minute time budget rather than reaching the 0.01 noise threshold. The frames are still visibly grainy. The budget is what stops a hard scene rendering forever; it is NOT evidence of convergence. A cleaner frame needs either more time or a different sampler, and neither was measured.
render_quality_settings.sidecars: With the denoiser on, V-Ray also writes <name>.denoiser.png and <name>.effectsResult.png next to the saved frame. Nothing in the collision map or the overwrite policy plans for them; they are now NAMED in the row detail and the log rather than silently left, and they are NOT deleted. Measured on 01 at 1200x900: mean neighbour-pixel difference 0.0444 in the saved .png against 0.0416 in .denoiser.png - so save_vfb_image saves the RGB channel and the denoised frame is the sidecar, about 7% cleaner. Whether save_vfb_image can be pointed at the denoised channel was NOT tried.

client_safe_output.source_of_truth: WR_ProposalScenes::NOTE_TAGS and ANNOT_TAGS = DIM_TAGS + NOTE_TAGS; WR_Mode manages ANNOT_TAGS from 1.9.3

client_safe_output.the_design_that_failed: OBSERVED live in run 1. Hiding the tags once at the top of the batch is undone by the very next unit, MODE -> DRAFT, because showing dimensions is draft mode's entire job - the plan export came out fully annotated. Hiding them AFTER the mode unit fixes the picture and breaks something worse: WR_Mode snapshots live tag visibility when it LEAVES a mode, so the model would have memorised "draft means no dimensions" permanently. The hide therefore brackets each EXPORT - no mode transition happens between a push and its pop.
client_safe_output.not_redundant_with_render_mode: On a model whose first-ever toggle happens inside the batch, WR_Mode's render snapshot is seeded from whatever was showing, which is everything. Render mode alone does not guarantee a clean frame on a fresh model.

defects_found.title: Hiding the annotation tags once per batch is undone by the very next unit
defects_found.detail: The obvious design - hide WR-Dims / WR-Dims-Doors / WR-Notes at the top of the unit list and restore them in finish - was written, run live, and the plan export still came out carrying the 20' and 16' strings and the ceiling banner. The unit immediately after the hide is [:mode, 'draft'], and DRAFT MODE'S WHOLE JOB IS TO SHOW DIMENSIONS. Moving the hide after the mode unit fixes the picture and introduces a worse bug: WR_Mode snapshots live tag visibility when it LEAVES a mode, so the model would have memorised 'draft means no dimensions' permanently.
defects_found.fix: The hide brackets each EXPORT (annot_push/annot_pop around write_image, and around render_production with the pop in finish). No mode transition occurs between a push and its pop, so no snapshot can record the temporary state.
defects_found.evidence: OBSERVED both ways: run 1's 05 Room Plan Top Down.png is fully annotated; run 2's, from the same scene and the same camera, carries nothing.

defects_found.title: finish's closing UI.messagebox can raise, leaving a finished batch claiming to run
defects_found.detail: The render-lane audit's F10 named UI.messagebox as the one residual raiser inside finish. It fired: under a scripted caller whose modals are muzzled, the line raised AFTER every file was written and every restore had run. The raise escaped finish into step's rescue, which called finish a SECOND time - so the mode restore ran twice - and @running was still latched true on a completed batch, so the next press hit the stale-reset path. Every file was on disk and the summary was correct; only the bookkeeping lied.
defects_found.fix: @running = false before the box, and the box rescued like every other UI call in the file.
defects_found.evidence: OBSERVED live, run 1: the dialog log shows the summary line, runFinished, then 'batch step raised: WhisperRoom::Bridge::ModalBlocked', then the summary line and runFinished AGAIN.

defects_found.title: The denoiser writes two unplanned sidecars, and the saved frame is the un-denoised channel
defects_found.detail: With /RenderChannelDenoiser enabled, V-Ray writes <name>.denoiser.png and <name>.effectsResult.png next to the frame save_vfb_image writes. Nothing in the collision map, the Ask/Overwrite/Skip policy or the summary knows they exist, so they accumulate in the output folder and could reach a client pack. Worse for quality: measured on 01 Booth Exterior Three-Quarter at 1200x900, mean neighbour-pixel difference is 0.0444 in the saved .png against 0.0416 in .denoiser.png - the saved file is the VFB's RGB channel and is about 7% noisier than the denoised result sitting beside it.
defects_found.fix: PARTIAL. save_frame now finds and NAMES the sidecars in the row detail and in the log rather than leaving them silently; it does not delete them, because deleting another program's output is not this tool's call. Pointing save_vfb_image at the denoised channel was NOT tried.

defects_found.title: Both renders ended on the six-minute budget, not on the noise threshold
defects_found.detail: progressive_threshold was set to 0.01 and progressive_maxTime to 6.0 minutes as a safety cap. Both renders ran the full budget, so 0.01 was NOT reached at 1200x900 on this machine and the frames are still visibly grainy. The budget is what stops a hard scene rendering forever; it is not evidence of convergence, and this pass did not measure what convergence would cost.
defects_found.fix: none - named so the next quality pass starts from a measured fact rather than a guess about whether the settings 'worked'.

defects_found.title: Sketchup.file_new on a dirty model raises a native modal the bridge cannot muzzle
defects_found.detail: The bridge muzzles UI::HtmlDialog#show and UI.messagebox, but Sketchup.file_new on a modified model puts up a native QMessageBox 'Save changes to Untitled?' that no Ruby-side muzzle can reach. It blocked SketchUp for about three minutes. The bridge DIAGNOSED IT CORRECTLY - exit 4, 'THE JOB STARTED AND SKETCHUP STOPPED ANSWERING ... the likely cause is A MODAL DIALOG' - which is exactly what that diagnosis is for, so this is a gap in coverage, not a failure of the design.
defects_found.fix: none. Cleared by invoking the dialog's 'No' button through Windows UI Automation - a named-button invoke, not blind keystrokes, and not the VFB or an HtmlDialog. A bridge-side file_new wrapper that refuses or pre-clears a dirty model would remove the need.

defects_found.title: The summary never reconciled rows planned against rows reported (pass 1's D8)
defects_found.detail: Pass 1 planned 5 rows, wrote 4 files, and said '4 exported, 0 skipped, 0 FAILED'. Nothing compared the plan to the results, so a row that produced no result at all was invisible.
defects_found.fix: start_run records @plan_files; summary_lines diffs it against the reported rows and names any that produced no result, calling it a lost row rather than a skip.

defects_found.where: scripts/rbparse.py's Ruby VM, and every pure method tested through it
defects_found.title: Float#to_f, Integer#to_i and NilClass#to_i do not exist in the offline test VM
defects_found.detail: rbparse.py boots SketchUp's own Ruby DLL into a barebones VM. In it, (10.5).to_f raises NoMethodError while 3.to_f returns 3.0, and nil.to_i and 1200.to_i raise too. Three of this pass's new pure methods failed their first offline run for exactly this reason and nothing else.
defects_found.fix: the pure methods use `x * 1.0` and `x.to_s.to_i` instead, with the reason in a comment. A .to_f in a pure method is a method that cannot be tested offline.

defects_found.title: The ambient downlights still cluster along one edge
defects_found.detail: In a 20' x 16' room, Soft density placed four ambient downlights at (40,48), (40,144), (120,48) and (200,48) - three of the four on the y=48 line. Better than pass 1 (which placed only two, both at x=40) but still not a grid. The booth keep-out does not explain the gap at (120,144) or (200,144).
defects_found.fix: none - carried forward from pass 1's D11.
